data.one_liner: D-pad navigation and focus management for Flutter TV apps.
data.what_it_does: Provides production-grade D-pad navigation, focus regions with memory, TV-correct directional traversal, and remote-key handling for Flutter applications targeting TV platforms. It replaces Flutter's default focus engine to properly support regions, beam-based traversal, edge controls, and remote semantics.
use_when: Building an app for Android TV, Fire TV, or Apple TV using Flutter.
Needing memory inside focus regions so returning to a row restores the previously selected item.
Managing complex spatial directional navigation and remote control inputs.
avoid_when: Building standard mobile or desktop applications that do not rely on remote control or D-pad input.
Needing advanced non-TV gamepad mechanics unrelated to spatial focus management.
strengths: Regions with memory that survive rebuilds and lazy lists.
Beam-based traversal mimicking real TV platforms like Android Leanback.
Built-in visual effects including animated flying highlights and custom focus states.
weaknesses: Specific to TV and D-pad/remote-controlled interfaces, rendering it largely irrelevant for typical touch-first mobile designs.
Requires wrapping the app and managing custom region components instead of relying purely on default Flutter focus nodes.
data.setup_notes: Wrap the root MaterialApp builder with Dpad.wrap().
data.minimal_example:
MaterialApp(
  builder: Dpad.wrap(),
  home: const HomePage(),
)
